twenty ninth sunday in ordinary time thirtieth sunday in ordinary time pray for catrrina houlihan, 14 sliabh cairn, whose funeral took place this saturday. 29th sunday : world mission sunday is the holy father’s annual appeal for spiritual and financial support so that the life-giving work of overseas mission and missionaries can continue. it always falls on the second last sunday in october, and like the good friday collection for the holy land and peter’s pence, it is one of three yearly universal church collections. world mission sunday collections take place in every single parish where the church is present including in poorer parishes in developing countries. it is a moment of universal solidarity when each member of the church family, regardless of location or background, play their part in supporting each other. this is what makes it such a special celebration. all offeri ngs and donations made become part of the holy father’s universal solidarity fund. this fund is a lifeline for struggling missionaries and the communities they serve across africa, asia and latin america, where over 1,100 mission dioceses are found. as these dioceses form and grow, so do their needs. on top of this, mission dioc eses are often in remote areas devastated by war and natural disasters, or where suppressed communities are just opening up to the life-saving message of jesus christ. this is why world mission sunday is so important. it offers young dioceses the financial and spiritual assistance they need to help their men, women, and children to survive and thrive. thu 22 : st john paul 11 was pope for over twenty-six years, from 22 october 1978 until his death on 2 april 2005. ordained bishop of krakow in 1958, he took a significant part in the second vatican council. as bishop of rome he visited almost all of the roman parishes and made apostolic journeys to 104 countries, including ireland, 29 september – 2 october 1979 grow in love - groarke sun25th oct 10.30am walter connell attracta mulderrig & walter connell t1: j. burke, mm gormley, walsh children’s corner : (loyola press) do you cheer a favourite sports team? the question the religious leaders asked jesus was whether the israelites should or should not pay taxes to caesar (the ruler of rome who controls israel). a trick question wanting to force jesus to pick a team: was jesus cheering for rome or the israelites? read today’s gospel mt 22:15 – 21. jesus points out that caesar’s image and name are on the money and says “give to caesar what is caesar’s and give to god what is god’s.” in other words, jesus was telling the phari sees that the image they wear is the team they are on – and the image we all wear is the image of god. the pharisees tried to stop jesus because they forgot what team they were actually on. we learn from jesus what it means to be on god’s team, we learn to share with others the same love, forgiveness, and healing that jesus offered to those around him. the more we do those same things as jesus did, the more we help others know they belong to god’s team, too. dear god, thank you for jesus, who reminds us that each of us belong to you and then shows us how to share your love with others. thank you and amen family prayer time: (loyola press) as your family gathers, make a list of the activities that your family spends time doing together, such as household tasks, jobs, academics, and recreational activities. talk about the importance of each of these activities and what would happen if there were an imbalance by spending too much time on one activity at the expense of another. in today’s gospel jesus speaks of the necessity of giving things their proper importance. read matt 22:15-21. the herodians and pharisees were giving too much importance to the issue of the payment of taxes. jesus says to them that loving and honouring god is of greater importance. in family life we do many important things, but we remember that god is of the greatest importance in our lives. pray that your family will learn to keep things in proper perspective, remembering to keep god first in your l ives. pray together today’s psalm, psalm 95. mission month: world mission sunday- our mission : send me, lord, out into the world that begins at my front door. may my every word flow from your heart and my actions be of love and peace that everything i do or say reflects your great mercy to all. help me witness to your truth no l ess in my silence than in my words and show me, lord, the way i should go. help me to see that my solemn duty to spread your gospel to everyone in the world is second only to their right to hear and respond to it. open my eyes to your presence in others and my ears to recognise your voice especially in the poor and oppressed. amen. if you're running late because getting everyone out the door was a battle, please still come to church. if your toddler won't sit still, please still come to church. if your baby needs to eat, please still come to church. if your child asks questions at the least convenient time, please still come to church. if someone cries, drops a toy, needs a snack, or has to make their third trip to the bathroom, please still come to church. if your child doesn't know all the words, all the prayers, or exactly when to sit and stand, please still come to church if you feel like you spent the entire mass managing your children and heard approximately 12% of the sermon, please still come to church. if sunday morning feels messy instead of peaceful, please still come to church if you're worried about, if you're worried your children are distracting the people around you, please still come to church. because children do not learn how to be part of the church by staying home they can sit quietly. they learn by being here. they learn the singing by hearing us sing. they learn the prayers by hearing us pray. they learn to worship by watching us worship. they learn that church is home because we make room for them here. the wiggles, whispers, dropped crayons, crying babies, and little voices are not interruptions to the life of the church. they are evidence that the church is alive. so bring the babies, bring the toddlers, bring the big kids, come late, sit at the back, sit in the front, step out where you need to. and come right back in. just come.
